claims.claim: Every A9 packing can be normalized into an 1188×839 subrectangle of A0.
claims.evidence: For fixed labels and orientations, the feasible coordinate set is compact: container bounds are compact and each pairwise non-overlap condition is a finite union of closed inequalities. Hence the sum of all left and top coordinates has a minimizer. If a rectangle with positive x-coordinate had no left-touching rectangle whose vertical interior overlaps it, the minimum of its finitely many positive clearances and its boundary clearance would permit a positive left translation, contradicting minimality. Following left blockers strictly decreases x and terminates at x=0; the analogous argument applies vertically. Thus every right and bottom endpoint is a nonnegative sum of 52s and 37s. Exact enumeration confirms that the largest representable endpoints within 1189 and 841 are respectively 1188 and 839, while 1189, 840, and 841 are not representable.
claims.search_method: Compactness and finite-clearance blocker-chain proof, followed by exhaustive nonnegative integer enumeration of 52i+37j.

claims.claim: There is an explicit packing of 516 sheets.
claims.evidence: The checker generated all 516 listed rectangles, confirmed each has dimensions 52×37 or 37×52, verified containment in 1188×839, and tested every pair for interior overlap. All assertions passed. The three families contain 60, 8, and 448 rectangles and meet only along boundaries.
claims.search_method: Exact generation, containment checks, and exhaustive pairwise integer interval-intersection tests.

claims.claim: No packing has 518 sheets; hence OPT≤517.
claims.evidence: After claim 0, it suffices to consider integer placements in 1188×839. For the marker rule x+y≡50 mod 52, a 52×37 rectangle contains exactly one marker in each of 37 rows, and a 37×52 rectangle exactly one in each of 37 columns. Exhausting all 52² origin-residue pairs for both orientations confirmed 37 markers per placement. Direct integer enumeration found 19,162 container markers. Giving each weight 1/37 yields total weight 19,162/37=517+33/37<518, while every sheet has weight 1; therefore an integral packing size is at most 517.
claims.witness: The weight certificate w(x,y)=1/37 when x+y≡50 (mod 52), and w(x,y)=0 otherwise, on the 1188×839 unit grid.
claims.search_method: Exact periodic exhaustion of every origin residue and direct enumeration of all marked container cells.

claims.claim: Any hypothetical 517-packing must span a maximum reduced dimension and contain a prescribed blocking chain.
claims.evidence: The occupied area is 517·52·37=994,708, exceeding 1187·838=994,706. Hence a normalized packing cannot have both rightmost endpoint at most 1187 and bottom endpoint at most 838; it reaches x=1188 or y=839. A rectangle reaching that boundary has a blocker path back to zero, including the terminal rectangle, whose widths or heights sum to the reached endpoint. Exhaustive Diophantine enumeration gives the unique representations 1188=20·52+4·37 and 839=14·52+3·37, establishing the stated chain compositions.
claims.witness: Boundary-chain arithmetic certificates 1188=20·52+4·37 and 839=14·52+3·37; each is the unique nonnegative representation.
claims.search_method: Exact area comparison combined with blocker-chain analysis and exhaustive nonnegative integer representation checks.

claims.claim: The natural horizontal 111+728 decomposition is exactly capped at 516.
claims.evidence: Area bounds the 1188×111 part by 68, attained by the first two coordinate grids. For 1188×728, exhaustive enumeration of all nonnegative line-intersection patterns found max(5h+7v)=98 under 37h+52v≤728 and max(7h+5v)=160 under 52h+37v≤1188. Summing the resulting inequalities gives 519N≤98·1188+160·728=232,904<519·449, so N≤448. A 32×14 grid of 37×52 rectangles attains 448. Thus the separated regions attain and cannot exceed 68+448=516.
claims.witness: The 68-sheet top construction from claim 1 together with (37i,52j;37,52), 0≤i<32 and 0≤j<14, in the translated 1188×728 lower region.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive integer enumeration of every feasible vertical- and horizontal-line pattern, followed by exact summed inequalities and construction verification.

claims.claim: The maximum size of a guillotine (slicing) A9-in-A0 packing is 516.
claims.evidence: Bottom-up compaction of a slicing tree preserves feasibility: vertical nodes add child widths and take their maximum height, while horizontal nodes take maximum width and add heights. Inductively both compact dimensions lie in the semigroup generated by 37 and 52, so an A0-fitting root is bounded by 1188×839. Conversely, every uniform-grid, slack, vertical-split, and horizontal-split DP transition constructs a valid slicing packing; structural induction shows every compacted slicing tree occurs in the recurrence. The exact integer DP exhausted 396 width and 204 height values when zero is included and returned G(1188,839)=516. The displayed construction is slicing: combine its two top grids vertically, then combine that 1188×111 block horizontally with the 1184×728 bottom grid.
claims.witness: A slicing tree with top children 1040×111 containing 60 sheets and 148×104 containing 8 sheets, combined above a 1184×728 grid containing 448 sheets; compact root 1188×839 with 516 leaves.
claims.search_method: Complete two-dimensional integer dynamic program over all semigroup dimensions and all exact horizontal and vertical splits, with an independent structural-induction completeness proof.

target_evidence: The exact target requires determining which one of 516, 517, and 518 is the global optimum. The verified placement and residue-weight certificate establish only 516≤OPT≤517. The remaining results impose necessary structure on a 517-packing and exclude fixed-split and slicing subclasses, but they do not exclude every nonslicing 517-packing or construct one. Thus the draft makes material, correct partial progress but does not fully resolve the target. Its headline and final section expressly retain the 516-versus-517 uncertainty and label the resolution PARTIAL, so the claimed resolution is accurate and not overclaimed.
